summary: Self-hostable story studio that turns a character and a short script into scene-by-scene AI video using your own provider keys.
whatItDoes: OpenHiggsfield Story Studio lets you pick a character or upload your own, write a short story, review the scenes and a cost estimate, and then generate the film with your own fal or Higgsfield credentials.
problem: Hosted AI video studios keep your drafts and keys on their side. This project gives you a studio you run yourself, with your own provider accounts and your own data.
whoFor: Creators who want to make short AI story videos
People who already pay for fal or Higgsfield and want their own studio
Developers who want a self-hosted video generation front end
whyChoose: It is MIT-licensed and self-hostable, stores provider keys encrypted, and keeps drafts, uploads and renders private to each workspace.
requirements: Node.js 24+ and FFmpeg on PATH (for local development)
Your own fal or Higgsfield credentials
An email service for sign-in links on a public deployment
overview: OpenHiggsfield Story Studio is an independent, self-hostable character-to-film studio. The README states clearly that it is not affiliated with, operated by, sponsored by or endorsed by Higgsfield.ai.

You choose from 50 characters or upload your own, write a one-minute story and review six scenes with narration directions and a generation estimate. When you're happy, you generate with your own provider credentials and watch each scene render, then get an assembled MP4.
Sign-in is by email magic link, accounts and workspaces are kept apart, and provider keys are encrypted at rest.

features.title: Character browser
features.body: Pick a built-in character or upload your own image, and keep private drafts you can delete.

features.title: Scene scripts and estimates
features.body: Review scene scripts, narration directions and a generation estimate before anything is spent.

features.title: Bring your own provider
features.body: Connect fal or Higgsfield; credentials are stored encrypted.

features.title: Render progress and MP4
features.body: See progress per scene, preview each clip and get the scenes assembled into one MP4.

features.title: Private workspaces
features.body: Accounts and workspaces are isolated, with email magic-link sign-in.

strengths: Provider keys are encrypted at rest
Provider tests use mocked requests and do not purchase generations
limitations: Public gallery publishing and private share links are not a complete production workflow yet
Voice and character consistency depend on the model you choose
Estimates are not final provider invoices
Keys are encrypted at rest, not end-to-end encrypted
Removing a draft does not remove completed films

A fal or Higgsfield account and credentials

steps.title: Generate an authentication secret
steps.body: Put the result in BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. Also set PUBLIC_ORIGIN, RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM, and either SIGNUP_EMAILS for invited users or ALLOW_SIGNUP=true for open registration.

steps.title: Start the studio
steps.body: Then open http://localhost:3000 and connect your provider under Connections after signing in.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.body: Needs Node.js 24+ and FFmpeg on PATH (set FFMPEG_PATH if needed).

steps.title: Start the studio in a second terminal
steps.body: Open http://127.0.0.1:5193. The local email screen offers a test sign-in link that only works on localhost.

environment.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
environment.description: Authentication secret; the README shows a node command to generate one.

environment.name: PUBLIC_ORIGIN
environment.description: The public address of your studio.

environment.name: EMAIL_FROM
environment.description: The address sign-in emails come from.

environment.name: SIGNUP_EMAILS
environment.description: Emails of invited users; or set ALLOW_SIGNUP=true for open registration.

firstRun.title: Sign in and connect a provider
firstRun.body: Open the studio, sign in with the email link, then add your fal or Higgsfield credentials under Connections. Don't put provider credentials in frontend source.

troubleshooting.problem: Video assembly fails in local development
troubleshooting.solution: Make sure FFmpeg is on PATH, or set FFMPEG_PATH.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in doesn't work on the hosted account flow
troubleshooting.solution: Email sign-in must be configured: set RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM.
